name: Vegetarian Chimichanga

ingredients.name: vegetarian melting cheese made with vegetarian coagulants

steps: Drain the cooked black beans and sweetcorn thoroughly. Heat 10 ml of the measured oil in a pan and cook onion and red pepper for 5 minutes until softened. Add cumin and smoked paprika for 30 seconds, then stir in beans, corn, cooked rice and salt. Cook 3 minutes until hot and fairly dry; cool for 10 minutes so the tortillas do not steam open.

Check the cheese label to ensure it contains no animal-derived coagulants. Stir the chopped coriander into the cooled filling. Briefly warm the four tortillas in a dry pan so they bend without cracking. Put one-quarter of the filling slightly below the centre of each tortilla, then add 35 g cheese and 25 g thick salsa. Leave a generous clear border.

Fold the left and right edges in over the filling, pull the near edge tightly across it, and roll into a sealed rectangular parcel. Place seam-side down. If necessary, secure with a wooden toothpick and remember to remove it before serving. Keep the salsa inside thick; liquid can cause dangerous spattering during frying.

Pour the remaining oil into a deep heavy pan, keeping it no more than half full, and heat to 175°C. Carefully lower in one or two parcels seam-side down; fry for 3–5 minutes, turning gently until all sides are crisp golden brown and the filling is hot. Return the oil to 175°C between batches.

Drain on a rack for 3 minutes and remove any toothpicks. Cut one chimichanga diagonally to check that the cheese has melted, then serve the four hot parcels with avocado slices and extra salsa if desired. The fried shell should be audibly crisp, unlike a soft burrito.
tips: This is a fried, tightly sealed tortilla parcel, not another name for a soft burrito. The reviewed image shows a crisp bubbled shell and beans, corn, rice, peppers and cheese in the cut centre. Keep both the filling and salsa fairly dry before frying.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
